headline: Bitcoin bounced back to about $64,500 on Sunday after briefly falling below $62,000, its lowest since mid-July, as about $2 billion of borrowed bets were force-closed and money kept leaving crypto funds.

market.asOf: CoinGecko coin pages read at about 07:55 UTC Sun 15 Nov (14:55 Bangkok). CoinMarketCap's bitcoin page showed a higher, apparently older figure ($66,619) at the same time. Prices move fast; use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: Extreme fear: CoinMarketCap's Fear and Greed Index showed 16 out of 100 when read on Sunday, and the Alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index was also in its extreme fear range.

stories.title: Bitcoin dips below $62,000, its lowest since July, then bounces as about $2B of borrowed bets are wiped out
stories.summary: Bitcoin slid in Asian trading on Sunday as traders who had borrowed to bet on rising prices were forced out automatically, and that forced selling pushed prices lower still. It then bounced back within about an hour, but is still down sharply on the week.
points: Bitcoin fell as low as $62,112 in Asia on Sunday, its weakest since July 14, per Bloomberg via Business Standard; Coinbase's low was $61,946, per CryptoTicker.
It rebounded to $65,098 within the hour, per CryptoTicker, and later traded near $64,500, per crypto.news.
About $2B of crypto bets were liquidated (force-closed) in the 24 hours to 9am Sunday Singapore time, including $774M in bitcoin and $488M in ether, per Coinglass data cited by Bloomberg.
Ether fell to $1,711, its lowest since July 8, per Bloomberg; it is about 63% below its record of $4,946, per CryptoTicker.
Bitcoin is down about 25% since 21 October and sits below its 200-day moving average, a widely watched long-term trend line, of about $73,000, per Bloomberg.

sources.label: Bloomberg via Business Standard: four-month low

stories.title: Money keeps leaving crypto: ETF withdrawals, shrinking stablecoins, and XRP below $1
stories.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs, the way many Americans hold bitcoin in a brokerage account, lost more than $1B for a second week. The supply of stablecoins, the digital dollars traders keep ready to buy coins, is shrinking fast. Both mean fewer buyers in the market.
points: Spot bitcoin ETFs had $1.07B of net outflows last week, the second straight week of more than $1B out, per The Block.
Spot ether ETFs lost $398.9M, their seventh straight losing week, per The Block.
Stablecoin supply fell $17B over the last month, the steepest drop since 2022, per Glassnode data cited by CoinDesk.
XRP fell to 89 cents, its lowest since November 2024, per CoinDesk.

stories.title: A near-certain December rate hike and a giant AI stock listing hang over the week
stories.summary: Higher interest rates make borrowing more expensive and tend to pull money away from riskier assets such as crypto. Futures markets expect the Fed to raise rates on 9 December. Some analysts also say Anthropic's huge stock listing this week may be drawing money away from crypto. These are market bets and opinions, not decisions.
points: CME FedWatch showed 88.5% odds of a quarter-point hike in December and 11.5% for a half-point hike, per Bitcoin.com News.
Anthropic and some existing shareholders plan to sell up to $64.4B of shares at $70 to $78 each, with Nasdaq trading under ANT due on 19 November, per The Next Web.
Bloomberg reported the Anthropic order books were "multiple times" oversubscribed, per StockAnalysis.
Price action "looks very similar to what happened through the SpaceX IPO pricing period," said Richard Galvin of DACM, per Bloomberg.

briefs.title: US moves to seize over $1.2B from the Binance hack
briefs.summary: A court approved the Justice Department's move to seize or restrain more than $1.2B stolen in the Binance hack, which it tied to North Korea, and efforts have frozen more than $2.7B, per The Block.

briefs.title: White House names new SEC and CFTC nominees
briefs.summary: The White House nominated Kristin Johnson and Steven Levine to the SEC and Nathan Anonick and Matthew Rowland to the CFTC, per The Block.

briefs.title: Solana's Breakpoint conference opens in London as SOL slumps
briefs.summary: Breakpoint runs 15-17 November at Olympia London. SOL hit an overnight low of $67.37 and was down about 20% on the week, per CryptoTicker.

briefs.title: Ethereum Foundation sells 7,500 ETH
briefs.summary: The Ethereum Foundation sold 7,500 ETH over four days for roughly $14.5M as ether fell, per Shattered.

briefs.title: Bitcoin trades into a modeled liquidation zone
briefs.summary: Glassnode's 11 November analysis placed the largest modeled cluster of forced-selling levels between $59,500 and $62,600, per Cryptonews.

briefs.title: Kava Lend hacked for about $3.8M
briefs.summary: An attacker drained about 55.2M KAVA through a dormant BUSD market, and the KAVA token fell nearly 40%, per The Block.

briefs.title: JPMorgan added to Strategy and bitcoin ETF holdings
briefs.summary: JPMorgan's third-quarter filing showed its Strategy stake up 36% and 11.4M shares of BlackRock's IBIT bitcoin ETF, per The Block.
